content.title: About
content.content: Raw cantaloupe is a juicy fruit with a green‑orange rind and bright orange flesh. Native to Southern Africa, it is now cultivated in warm regions worldwide. Cantaloupe offers a sweet, mildly fragrant flavor and a soft, tender texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cantaloupe belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family, making it a close relative of cucumbers, zucchini, and pumpkins.
The fruit is composed of more than 90 % water, making it an excellent hydrator in hot weather.
Its orange flesh gets its color from high beta‑carotene levels, a precursor of vitamin A.
Cantaloupe seeds are edible after roasting and are rich in healthy fats.
Ancient cultures used cantaloupe in rituals and as a symbol of fertility.

items.title: Rich in vitamin A
items.content: Beta‑carotene in cantaloupe converts to vitamin A, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C provides antioxidant protection and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Hydration support
items.content: High water content helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Heart‑friendly potassium
items.content: Potassium contributes to normal blood pressure and heart function.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cantaloupe.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Natural sugars give cantaloupe its sweetness; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: If grown with conventional methods, pesticide residues may remain on the rind; thorough washing is recommended.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cantaloupe is enjoyed fresh, cut into cubes or wedges. It can be added to fruit salads, smoothies, yogurts, and desserts. The rind is typically not eaten, but the peeled fruit can be used in marinades.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store whole cantaloupe at room temperature for up to 2–3 days. Once cut, place pieces in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to 5 days. Discard if soft spots or off‑odors develop.
